analysis:
The visible changes affect only provider-local supervision. In ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (head 429-430), the connection-control reader now calls noteCoordinatorRequest() for .inferenceRequest before passing the event to the unchanged work FIFO. noteCoordinatorRequest (ServingAuthorizationRecovery patch, head ~17-20) sets coordinatorConnection.lastRequestAt, but only while connected. It does not admit, decrypt or route anything, and the request path (admitInWorkFIFO -> handleInferenceRequest) is unchanged. The A-001 encryption path, the fixed X25519 resume responder (A-003, T-053) and the attestation provider are also unchanged; base and head lines 568-620 are identical apart from the line shift.

superviseServingAuthorization now switches on ServingReadiness.verdict(connection:trust:now:) instead of hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization/path=="legacy" plus UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.connectionLacksAuthorization. Its outcomes are logging, unauthorizedSince/unauthorizedReconnectAttempts bookkeeping and requestPlannedReconnect(). These are availability and diagnostics (TB-011, T-057, A-018), not serving permission. Authorization is coordinator-owned (A-016, T-052), so a provider-local verdict that is wrong cannot grant trust. The coordinator is trusted, so a routed request is a reasonable liveness signal. Shadow/trust events still bypass the slow FIFO.

Uncertainties for integration:
(1) ServingReadiness is not in this batch. Its handling of lastRequestAt versus a refusal timestamp, and its .pending/.unconfirmed cases, need checking. Pending/unconfirmed now clears unauthorizedSince, so they never accumulate toward reconnect recovery. If expired App Attest authorization maps to .unconfirmed rather than .blocked, a refused provider could stop self-recovering (T-057 availability regression).
(2) unauthorizedReconnectAttempts now resets only on .authorized; the earlier explicit legacy-path reset depends on how ServingReadiness treats path=="legacy".
(3) Whether status/doctor display lastRequestAt as "authorized" in a way that overclaims trust (T-056, T-058).

No concrete regression was established from the visible source.
